scene black
I think I’ve done enough for today.
In fact, this is probably the most I’ve done at all since I was in the shape and state required to attend similar events hosted by my class.
I wonder how those work without me.
But that shouldn’t come as much of a surprise as my narcissism seldom allows me to comprehend how anything works without me.
Even acknowledging that, though, I can’t help but feel like there’s something missing despite everything I’ve accomplished during my brief time here.
It was just one day, but it felt like two. So is this sudden and apparent emptiness the result of me wanting to stretch that two into a three? Maybe a three into a four?
I shrug my shoulders as I unzip the mouth of my shelter and allow it to swallow me.
Everyone else has hurried off to sleep already and I look on in awe as my niece is digested before my very eyes.
I don’t call her my daughter internally because it still hasn’t set in yet.
All I know is that she’s cute. And so I watch her sleep for approximately seven minutes before opening up a second mouth inside of the mouth and crawling into that one.
I think I like camping.
I think I like being out here where the only people I can hurt are people who have already been hurt before.
It alleviates some of the pressure of simply existing and grants me the strength I need to not be chewed in half by my sleeping bag.
When I close my eyes, I think of Heaven.
I think of how it must appear. Or if it ever will appear. Because I want it to appear.
But I also worry that days like this are the closest I’ll ever come to experiencing such a thing.
My final thought before falling asleep is that I want to do this again.
I just want to do it alone next time.
I want to be one with the forest.
I want it to swallow me.
Goodnight, Moon.

scene sky
: Is it faster if I take this left?
: That road’s closed for construction. But you can follow this one straight for three more lights and then turn left at that one.
: Weird. I don’t remember seeing any construction at all on our way to pick you guys up.
: You were probably just so excited to spend time with your newest daughter that you overlooked it.
: What are they even building over here? It’s not another porn shop is it? Am I going to have to fight another small business owner to defend my turf? You’ll help- won’t you, Haru-kun?
: Sure, Maki. I’ll fight a rival porn dealer for you.
: I’ll help too! I can be scrappy.
: No, you’re too small. You’ll only get in the way.
: I hadn’t noticed any of this either. Do you know what’s going on, Ami?
: Mm...just more houses, I think? Maybe a closer convenience store if we’re lucky.
: That sure sounds like it’d be convenient to me.
: Maki, drive faster.
: Maki, don’t.
: But if we don’t get there soon, Sara might try to make another joke.
: Was that a joke? I thought it was more of an observation than anything.
: It was obviously a joke! It’s not my fault that none of you appreciate good humor. Right, Ami?
: Hm? What was the joke? I must have missed it.
: Ugh! Never mind! Maki, drive faster!
It’s the morning after, if you couldn’t already tell.
Our trip has come to an end and the time has come for us to bid farewell to camaraderie and get back to our old, boring lives.
I’m starting to think mine might be a little less boring from now on, though. But there’s still one problem-
I don’t know what to do about Niki.
I’ve obviously had several chances to talk to Ami about her proposition but, I...may have prioritized something else.
Something with a more immediate impact on the way I’m thinking as opposed to something that would have to take place in the future.
I’m pretty sure that’s okay, though. And I’m pretty sure Niki would be proud of me for taking the step I took last night.
I know Ami’s proud of me, that’s for sure. But I also know that she’d be proud of me if I decided I was a cat one day and started dropping dead mice at her feet.
Suffice it to say, her pride comes easy. Niki’s comes at a cost.
And mine is a giant invisible force-field covering every inch of my body in a way that makes me forget it’s even there.
scene black
When we pull up to the house, Sara gets out of the car as well and follows Ami and me to the door.
Originally, I think it’s just to give her the chance to say goodbye and...hug us or whatever. But I quickly realize that’s not the case when Maki speeds off.
She smiles at me, silently asking to be invited in. So I silently respond by opening the door as a low-effort way to repay her for opening one yesterday.
scene saraamishouse1
: Did you have fun yesterday, Ami?
: Yeah...and thanks again for making me...not so hideous anymore.
: Thank me again once you can get rid of those dark circles. Or just come visit me so I can see the finished product.
: Maybe don’t invite my niece out to the bar, Sara.
scene saraamishouse2
: You’re still calling her that after yesterday? Did we fail our mission after all?
: Oh. Shit.
: It’s fine. I imagine it’ll take some getting used to. Besides, it’s not like you’re technically wrong. And I don’t really care what you call me.
: We can...take it slow or...
scene saraamishouse3
: Yeah...
: Are you doing anything later tonight, Ami? Maybe you, me, and Sana could go out to dinner or something? That wouldn’t be too weird, would it?
scene saraamishouse4
: Maybe another time. I already told one of my friends I’d meet up with them and...probably shouldn’t immediately back out.
: Wait, you did? Are you sure you’re ready for that? It’s not too soon? You don’t want to...stay inside for a few more days?
scene saraamishouse5
: Weren’t you literally just trying to get me to start leaving the house again yesterday? I’m a burden to you if I stay here and we both know that.
: But that still doesn’t mean I expect you to start acting normal again after one outing and-
: It’s fine. It’s just Maya I’m meeting up with anyway.
scene nodokontest6
scene saraamishouse5
: Ah.
scene saraamishouse6
: Then maybe me and you could go out to dinner?
: Sara, I like you. And I want to thank you again for yesterday. But please — don’t push it.
scene saraamishouse7
: Hey, you were my first pick! Sensei’s just the backup! You know where my heart really lies!
scene saraamishouse8
: That’s only because the quickest way to a man’s heart is through his daughter. And if you win me over, you think you’ll win him as well. Don’t think I don’t know your games, Sara.
: Can I not want both of those things? Why does it have to be one or the other?
: Just give it a rest, Sara. Ami’s not letting you out of this one.
: Right you are, Dad.
scene saraamishouse9
: You can have him for a few minutes, though. I’m gonna go warm the bath up.
: Camping is fun and all, but I think I would have preferred a hot spring instead.
: Hahah...I’ll try to remember that for next time...
scene saraamishouse10

Ami exhibits an extreme amount of growth by leaving me in the room with a woman my age. Either that or she’s cynically and slyly expressing her doubt that I’m sexually interested in older women to begin with.
Either way, the two of us are left alone as she runs into her room to grab a change of clothes for the bath. But I guess she’s never been that opposed to Sara in the first place.
And while I want to sit here and ponder why that seems to be the case, I’m worried that doing so will lead me down a road I don’t want to think of at all.
So I match the tone set by a local bartender and also stand here in silence, waiting for that quiet to be killed off and replaced with something brighter.
: Uhh...
: Welp...I need to head out.
: You do? I figured you’d be sticking around for a little while longer considering how you followed us in here.
scene saraamishouse11
: I really just wanted to say goodbye to Ami. But this is your first day as father and daughter and I probably shouldn’t be getting in the way of that.
: It might be the first day in name, but Ami pointed out yesterday that that’s sort of how things have been all along.
: But hey, maybe now I’ll start making better decisions when it comes to her guidance.
: I probably won’t, but it’s worth a shot.
scene saraamishouse12
: I know exactly what you mean. I made a ton of mistakes with Sana when she was growing up that I didn’t realize until way later. Heck, even now I’m making mistakes.

: But we’re only human, Sensei. Being perfect is so far out of the question that all we can really do is hope those mistakes don’t pile up to the point where our girls can’t figure out how to get over them.
: That’s why I wanted to help with Ami. I know what that fear is like.
scene saraamishouse13
: But I guess she’s also right about the “wanting to win you over” part.
if sarasex == False:
: Sara-
scene saraamishouse14
: I know, I know. Your heart lies elsewhere.
: I just wanted to remind you of the life you’re missing out on. That’s all.
scene saraamishouse15
: But I’ll be going now.
: I had fun yesterday, Sensei. Even if I was just living in a fantasy for part of it.
: I hope you did too.
scene black
: And good luck with Ami. Feel free to let me know if you need anything.
: I will. Thanks, Sara.
: And come visit sometime! We miss your face. And your money.
: I will. I’ll talk to you later.
: Bye! See you soon!
Sara exits the house and I-
Well, I guess my new-ish life begins.
scene bedroom_day
There’s no way of knowing if this change in my relationship with Ami will actually affect anything, but...I’m going to have to find out eventually.
else:
: I figured as much. But some might say you’ve already won.
scene saraamishouse15
: And some might say I haven’t. It really comes down to what you’ll do next, Sensei. I’ve done more than enough to prove I’d make an excellent rock for your garden.
: Probably not the best analogy, Sara. Most gardens have more than one rock in them.
: As long as I’m the biggest and the one you look at first, I’m happy.
: Maybe a boulder would be better then. Something you wouldn’t be able to move.
scene saraamishouse14
: But I digress. And now I really have overstayed my welcome.
scene black
Sara gives me a quick hug before retreating to the door.
But when she grabs the handle, I feel the urge to call out to her.
scene saraamishouse16
: You haven’t overstayed your welcome, Sara.
: You can come here whenever you want.
: I mean it.
: You’ve been a huge help. And it’s nice having someone on hand who at least sort of knows what they’re doing when it comes to raising a teenager.
: So yeah, drop by whenever.
: We’d both be happy to see you.
: Is something wrong. Why are you just-
scene black
: That’s not something you should have said to me.
: But...why not?
: I don’t get it.
: Sensei...if you let me come here whenever I want...
scene saraamishouse17
: I’d never leave!
: Sara?...
scene saraamishouse18
: At least not without you two.
: You...
: You’re...not saying you want to move in, are you?
scene saraamishouse19
: Here? I guess we could make it work if we tried hard enough.
: It might be a little small for four people, but...I don’t need a lot of space. And I’m sure Sana and Ami wouldn’t mind sharing a room for a few years. But if that’s not possible...
scene saraamishouse17
: What about the future?
: What about the future, Sara?
scene saraamishouse20
: I’ve been thinking about leaving this place.
: And when I do, I want you to come with me. Ami too, of course.
: Somewhere the four of us can be a family. Somewhere on the other side of the wall.
: But...we have no way of knowing when that wall will be gone.
: But wouldn’t it be nice to have something to look forward to when it does?
scene saraamishouse17
: Maybe somewhere in the countryside so we could go camping a little more often! Doesn’t that sound great?
: I mean...yeah. But-
: A family?...
scene saraamishouse21
: Ami?...How long have you-
: You want the four of us...to be a family?
: Or more! I’m still young. I wouldn’t mind having another.
: With who?
scene saraamishouse22
: Seriously?
: Okay, I guess that’ll just be a topic for another day! But apart from another child, how does that sound to you, Ami?
: Are you okay with leaving Kumon-mi behind? Or would you rather stay here? Because the more I think about it, the more I want to get away.
: And I don’t think there’s anything that would make me happier than taking you two with me.
scene saraamishouse23
: Well...what do you have to say about this?
: This is all just hypothetical for now, guys. We obviously can’t go anywhere yet.
: And I don’t want it to sound like I’m trying to force myself into your family or...take the place of anyone, but...
: It’s just something to think about.
: I think the four of us could have a nice life together.
: Dad?
scene black
: I think we need to have another talk soon, Ami.
Sara exits the house and I-
I guess I have one more thing to add to the conversation about Niki that I’ve been fearfully avoiding.
But despite how the weight of these two options presses so heavily against my chest that I can feel the ghost of an old worm, there is one positive to come from them.
It’s the idea that there are people who will love my niece even if I’m gone.
Sorry.
Daughter.
scene bedroom_day
But apart from that...I guess it’s time to try and force a little more normalcy back into my life as well.
Even if it’s just one step at a time.
